title: Understand Mixed Numbers as Wholes Plus Parts
concept: Identify the whole-number part and fractional part of a mixed number and explain what each part represents.
prerequisites: Understand denominator as equal parts per whole
templates: Match a mixed number to a shaded model
Identify the whole and fractional parts of a mixed number
Count complete wholes plus remaining equal parts
Choose the mixed number for a real-world quantity
remediationNotes: Rebuild the number from complete wholes first, then name the leftover equal parts. Ask the student to verbalize the whole count before the fractional part.
recheckTemplates: Given a model with complete wholes and one partial whole, write the mixed number.
Explain what the whole-number part and fractional part mean in a context.
parentTutorNotes: A mixed number is one number made from complete wholes plus part of the next whole. Ask the student to point to the wholes before naming the fraction.

title: Count Unit Fraction Parts in a Mixed Number
concept: Convert a mixed number into the total count of unit fractions it contains.
prerequisites: Understand mixed numbers as wholes plus parts
Know each whole contains denominator-sized unit parts
templates: Find how many unit fractions are in a mixed number
Fill the total count of thirds, fourths, fifths, or sixths
Interpret a story quantity as unit fractions
Count unit parts from a model
remediationNotes: Represent each whole as a full group of denominator-sized unit parts, then add the leftover numerator.
recheckTemplates: Given a mixed number, find the total number of unit fraction parts.
Show the grouped calculation used to count the unit fraction parts.
parentTutorNotes: This is the foundation for mixed-to-improper conversion. Listen for the student saying how many parts are in each whole.

title: Simplify the Fractional Part of a Mixed Number
concept: Simplify the fraction in a mixed number while keeping the whole-number part unchanged.
prerequisites: Understand that equivalent fractions have the same value
templates: Write a mixed number in simplest form
Fill missing numerator and denominator after simplifying
Identify equivalent mixed numbers
Choose the simplest equivalent mixed number
remediationNotes: Temporarily isolate the fractional part, simplify it using a common factor, then restore the unchanged whole-number part.
recheckTemplates: Simplify a mixed number with a reducible fractional part.
Name the common factor used to simplify the fractional part.
parentTutorNotes: The whole number is not reduced. The student should only simplify the fraction after the whole number.

title: Place Mixed Numbers on a Number Line
concept: Locate a mixed number between whole numbers by partitioning the interval into equal fractional parts.
prerequisites: Read whole-number positions on a number line
Partition an interval into equal parts
templates: Mark a mixed number on a number line
Read a plotted point as a mixed number
Choose the whole-number interval containing a mixed number
Complete missing tick labels
remediationNotes: Anchor at the whole-number part first, split only the next interval into equal parts, then count forward to the fractional part.
recheckTemplates: Identify a mixed number from an unlabeled point between two whole numbers.
Place a named mixed number on a partitioned number line.
parentTutorNotes: This checks whether the student sees mixed numbers as locations. Ask which two whole numbers the value sits between.

title: Understand Improper Fractions as More Than One Whole
concept: Recognize improper fractions as total counts of equal parts that can exceed one whole.
templates: Match an improper fraction to a model
Count shaded unit parts across more than one whole
Classify a fraction as less than, equal to, or greater than one
Write an improper fraction from a visual model
remediationNotes: Build one whole as denominator-over-denominator, then add extra unit parts and count the total numerator.
recheckTemplates: Given several complete wholes plus a partial whole, write the improper fraction.
Explain why a fraction with numerator greater than denominator can be valid.
parentTutorNotes: An improper fraction is valid. It counts equal parts, even when the total passes one whole.

title: Convert Mixed Numbers to Improper Fractions
concept: Use the whole number, denominator, and numerator to find the total count of equal fractional parts.
prerequisites: Count unit fraction parts in mixed numbers
templates: Convert a mixed number to an improper fraction
Complete the missing numerator in an improper fraction
Convert a story quantity into an improper fraction
Explain the conversion from a model
remediationNotes: Connect the shortcut to grouped unit parts: wholes create full groups, then leftover parts are added. Keep the denominator unchanged.
recheckTemplates: Convert a mixed number with denominator 3, 4, 5, or 6 to an improper fraction.
Show the grouped calculation or model behind the conversion.
parentTutorNotes: The denominator stays the same because the part size stays the same. Only the number of parts changes.

title: Convert Improper Fractions to Mixed Numbers
concept: Divide the numerator by the denominator to form complete wholes and a remaining fractional part.
templates: Convert an improper fraction to a mixed number
Fill quotient and remainder in a conversion
Group a model into complete wholes
Choose the equivalent mixed number
remediationNotes: Group the numerator into sets the size of the denominator. Full groups become the whole number and leftovers become the numerator.
recheckTemplates: Convert an improper fraction with a nonzero remainder to a mixed number.
Explain the meaning of the quotient and remainder in the answer.
parentTutorNotes: The student is regrouping parts into wholes. Ask how many full wholes can be made and what remains.

title: Match Equivalent Mixed and Improper Forms
concept: Recognize and produce equivalent mixed-number, improper-fraction, and model representations of the same quantity.
prerequisites: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions
Convert improper fractions to mixed numbers
templates: Match mixed and improper forms
Choose all equivalent representations
Complete a representation table
Find and correct a conversion error
remediationNotes: Use a three-column organizer for model, mixed number, and improper fraction. Verify each by counting the same unit parts.
recheckTemplates: Given one representation, produce the other two equivalent forms.
Select the matching form from distractors with similar digits.
parentTutorNotes: This checks flexibility. The student should be able to change form without changing value.

title: Compare Mixed Numbers with Like Denominators
concept: Compare mixed numbers by whole-number part first and fractional part second when denominators match.
prerequisites: Compare proper fractions with the same denominator
templates: Choose the greater or lesser mixed number
Fill an inequality symbol
Compare story quantities
Explain the comparison using whole part then fraction part
remediationNotes: Compare whole-number parts first. If those match, compare fractional numerators because the denominator means the part size is the same.
recheckTemplates: Compare pairs where whole-number parts differ.
Compare pairs where whole-number parts match and fractional numerators differ.
parentTutorNotes: Use a two-step comparison: whole numbers first, fractional parts second.

title: Compare Improper Fractions with Common Denominators
concept: Compare improper fractions by making the part sizes the same, then comparing numerators.
templates: Compare two improper fractions
Complete equivalent fractions before comparing
Fill an inequality symbol
Select the larger amount from two models
remediationNotes: Name the part size first. If part sizes differ, rewrite both fractions with a shared denominator before comparing numerators.
recheckTemplates: Compare two improper fractions with unlike denominators.
Show the common-denominator rewrite before choosing the greater value.
parentTutorNotes: The student is comparing fairly by using same-sized parts. Ask to see both rewritten fractions before the decision.

title: Compare Mixed Numbers and Improper Fractions
concept: Compare values written in different forms by converting to a shared representation.
prerequisites: Convert between mixed numbers and improper fractions
templates: Compare a mixed number with an improper fraction
Choose a conversion strategy
Fill an inequality symbol
Identify the more efficient comparison route
remediationNotes: Choose one comparison lane: convert both to improper fractions or both to mixed numbers. Estimate size before writing the inequality symbol.
recheckTemplates: Compare one mixed number and one improper fraction that are close in value.
Require conversion plus an inequality statement.
parentTutorNotes: Different forms can describe the same quantity. The comparison is fair only after both values are interpreted in a compatible way.

title: Order Mixed and Improper Fractions
concept: Order three or more values that may include mixed numbers, improper fractions, and whole-number equivalents.
templates: Arrange values from least to greatest
Place values on a number line
Identify the greatest or smallest value
Repair an incorrectly ordered list
remediationNotes: Convert all values into one chosen form, annotate approximate size, then order. Use a number line when values are close.
recheckTemplates: Order four values containing mixed, improper, and whole-number forms.
Justify why the first value is smallest and the last value is greatest.
parentTutorNotes: This is a synthesis skill. The student must choose a strategy, preserve equivalent values, and compare several numbers consistently.
